claims.text: Single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys can exhibit an extraordinary balance of strength and ductility relative to conventional alloys.
During high-strain-rate deformation, SRO facilitates rapid and coordinated dislocation nucleation.
During high-strain-rate deformation, SRO facilitates coordinated propagation of dislocations.
Partial dislocations contribute to deformation in single-phase FCC entropy alloys.
CrCoNi is a single-phase FCC alloy.
CrCoNi can possess measurable short-range order.
SRO stabilizes specific dislocation or planar-fault configurations.
SRO promotes spatially uniform slip.
SRO-enabled coordinated dislocation nucleation and motion reduce local stress concentrations.
The proposed coordinated dislocation motion sustains work hardening.
The proposed SRO-mediated mechanism delays localized failure under dynamic loading.
At high strain rates, the HEA will develop more uniform dislocation structures than a conventional FCC alloy lacking pronounced SRO.
At high strain rates, the HEA will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than the conventional-alloy baseline.
At high strain rates, the HEA will sustain work hardening and delay localized failure relative to the conventional-alloy baseline.
Pure Ni or a low-SRO steel provides a conventional FCC baseline lacking pronounced SRO.
The mechanism should apply to single-phase FCC entropy alloys with measurable SRO.
The mechanism should apply primarily to alloys with moderate to high stacking-fault energy.
The mechanism should hold from approximately 10^2 to 10^4 s^-1 near room temperature.
The quantitative influence of SRO on dislocation dynamics at extreme strain rates and varying temperatures remains unresolved.
Failure to observe either more uniform coordinated dislocation evolution or distinguishable work hardening and delayed failure would falsify the proposed SRO mechanism.

contradictions.description: CrCoNi is presented as the exemplar initial material, but the boundary requires moderate-to-high stacking-fault energy, whereas the cited CrCoNi evidence reports a negative calculated stacking-fault energy and high twinning propensity.
